stories.title: Developers File Plans for 402-Unit Housing Project Along Astoria Waterfront
stories.excerpt: A pair of Astoria developers has filed plans to build 402 housing units in the World’s Borough. Dominick Acquista and Lorenzo Devardo, under the shell corporation Across the River Realty Development, filed plans to replace three industrial buildings at 31-29 Vernon Boulevard in Astoria, Queens, with a 20-story residential tower, according to city records. The New York Business Journal first reported the filing. The LLC filed plans with the New York City Planning Commission on Wednesday seeking a zoning change and text amendment to allow it to build housing above the current height restrictions. The land targeted for redevelopment sits just across Vernon Boulevard from Socrates Sculpture Park and the East River beyond that. Acquista and Devardo could not be reached for comment. Of the 402 units, about 100 of them would be affordable apartments under the city’s Mandatory Inclusionary Housing requirements for those making 60 percent of the area median income. The proposed Astoria project would also feature 10,108 square feet of commercial space and 3,069 square feet of community facility space, as well as 26 parking spaces, the application shows. Other buildings of similar size are being planned for Astoria as well. The Domain Companies secured a $175 million construction loan to build 429 units at 35-45, 35-33 and 35-42 41st Street in August. In September, Moses Freund’s Vaja Group purchased a former Staples building at 24-41 31st Street for $26 million with plans to construct a 108-unit mixed-use development. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Across the River Realty Development files 402-unit, 20-story tower in Astoria, Queens
100 units (25%) affordable at 60% AMI via Mandatory Inclusionary Housing
Zoning change sought to override current height restrictions on Vernon Boulevard site
stories.summary: Developers Dominick Acquista and Lorenzo Devardo filed plans with NYC Planning Commission to replace three industrial buildings at 31-29 Vernon Boulevard in Astoria, Queens with a 402-unit residential tower. The project includes ~100 affordable units, 10,108 SF of commercial space, and 3,069 SF of community facility space, plus 26 parking spaces. The site sits across from Socrates Sculpture Park with East River views, requiring a zoning text amendment to permit residential above current height limits.
stories.impact: Astoria waterfront rezoning signals NYC's continued conversion of industrial/commercial land to residential, expanding multifamily supply in an undersupplied outer-borough market. Mandatory inclusionary housing dilutes project returns but enables transit-proximate, waterfront-adjacent density; watch whether MIH ramp forces lower market-rate rents or higher presale pricing to offset affordability drag. Entitlement risk is material given zoning variance required.

stories.title: Legion Investment Group, SMA Equities Pair on 300K-SF UES Resi Project
stories.excerpt: Legion Investment Group and SMA Equities have teamed on a 300,000-square-foot residential development rising on Manhattan’s Upper East Side. The new partnership secured a $99 million pre-development loan for the 37-story project at 1491-1497 Third Avenue on Thursday, according to The Real Deal, which first reported the news. BDT & MSD Partners and Deutsche Bank provided the loan, while a Walker & Dunlop team led by Aaron Appel, Dustin Stolly, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer and Sean Bastian arranged the financing. “We’re pleased to once again partner with Legion, alongside SMA Equities, to arrange the financing that facilitated the acquisition of this irreplaceable Upper East Side condominium development site,” Appel said in a statement to CO. The assemblage at the corner of East 84th Street and Third Avenue has been nearly 20 years in the making, according to TRD. Samy Mahfar’s SMA Equities first purchased the corner lot at 1491-1493 Third Avenue in 2007, paying $33.8 million for the historic commercial building alongside real estate investor David Moussazadeh and Rex Properties’ Francis Moezinia. In 2016, the three partners secured the taller commercial property at 1495 Third Avenue next door for $18.2 million, according to city reports, and snapped up the five-story mixed-use apartment building at 1497 Third Avenue for $12.5 million in 2025. Demolition for the residential development is already underway, with Hill West Architects selected for its design. The forthcoming 510-foot-tall tower will include roughly 120 condos, according to New York YIMBY, and will offer 18,994 square feet of lower-level commercial space. The project with SMA Equities adds another feather to the cap of Legion’s Upper East Side portfolio, which includes luxury condominium towers at 109 East 79th Street and 1122 Madison Avenue. The latter development with Nahla Capital topped out in January. This past summer, Legion also wrapped vertical construction
bullets: Legion Investment Group and SMA Equities secure $99M pre-dev loan for 37-story UES condo tower
300,000 SF mixed-use project at 1491-1497 Third Avenue, East 84th Street corner
20-year land assembly completed; BDT & MSD Partners and Deutsche Bank finance
stories.summary: Legion Investment Group and SMA Equities partnered on a 300,000-square-foot, 37-story residential development on Manhattan's Upper East Side, securing a $99 million pre-development loan from BDT & MSD Partners and Deutsche Bank via Walker & Dunlop. The site at the corner of East 84th Street and Third Avenue represents a nearly 20-year assemblage that began when SMA Equities acquired the corner lot in 2007 for $33.8 million.
stories.impact: UES condo financing at $99M pre-dev loan underscores persistent capital availability for prime Manhattan mixed-use development despite broader rate headwinds; suggests lender confidence in high-income residential demand and condo conversion economics in the submarket. Completion of two-decade assemblage removes land-use friction and signals near-term conversion to rental or condo supply on a premium corridor; expect presale momentum to influence broader Manhattan pricing signals.

stories.title: Harbor Associates Sells Office Campus in North L.A. County for $32M
stories.excerpt: Strauss Investments has acquired a smaller two-building office campus in northern Los Angeles County for $32 million. The San Diego-based investor purchased Commons at Valencia, a 157,189-square-foot Class A office property in Santa Clarita’s Valencia neighborhood from Harbor Associates, according to CBRE, which represented the seller. The deal is equal to about $204 per square foot. Commons at Valencia spans nearly 9 acres at 25124 and 25152 Springfield Court, just off Interstate 5, in Valencia in the Santa Clarita Valley. It includes two three-story buildings and a two-story parking structure with 625 spaces. The campus, built in 2005, is 79 percent leased with tenants in professional services, insurance, financial services and real estate industries. Harbor completed an extensive renovation in 2020. “Commons at Valencia attracted significant investor interest due to its strong tenant roster, recent capital improvements and strategic location within one of Southern California’s premier suburban office markets,” CBRE Senior Vice President Mark Shaffer said in a statement. “The property’s leasing momentum and long-term growth prospects within the Valencia submarket created a compelling investment opportunity for the buyer.” Shaffer represented Harbor in the sale alongside CBRE’s Anthony DeLorenzo, Sean Sullivan and Gerard Poutier. Valencia has remained one of the stronger-performing office submarkets in north L.A. County, according to CBRE, with persistent growth in its residential and employment bases. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Strauss Investments acquires Commons at Valencia office campus for $32M ($204/SF)
157,189 SF Class A campus in Santa Clarita, 79% leased, built 2005, renovated 2020
Two 3-story buildings, 625-space parking on 9 acres near I-5
stories.summary: Strauss Investments, a San Diego-based investor, acquired Commons at Valencia, a 157,189-square-foot Class A office campus in Santa Clarita's Valencia neighborhood from Harbor Associates for $32 million ($204/SF). The 2005-built, recently renovated property spans 9 acres with two three-story buildings, is 79% leased to professional services, insurance, financial services and real estate tenants, and includes 625 parking spaces.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. Office-to-residential conversion economics in Santa Clarita remain challenged by suburban location, logistics-tenant rooted tenancy, and limited transit; no signal of near-term mixed-use redevelopment. Monitor only if Santa Clarita sees rapid employer in-migration (aerospace, tech hubs) that could trigger office-to-resi conversion discussion.

stories.title: Prestige Companies Buys Back Dania Beach, Fla., Residential Complex at a Discount
stories.excerpt: A condominium community in Dania Beach, Fla., has traded for $27.3 million in a deed-in-lieu of foreclosure, which is nearly $10 million less than its previous sale price, buyer Prestige Companies said Thursday. Prestige Companies and MV Real Estate Holdings are the new owners of Atlantica at Dania Beach at 624 Northeast Second Street. The project consists of 124 one- and two-bedroom condos. Prestige acquired 118 of those units. Call it a boomerang deal: Prestige was the original developer of Atlantica at Dania Beach. The project was completed in 2024 as an apartment community, and Prestige sold the project to S2 Dania Property for $36.75 million. That owner took a $30 million loan and planned to convert the 124 rentals into condos. However, S2 Dania Property sold only six of those units. Prestige Companies saw an opportunity to buy back its former asset at a discount. “We’ve always been confident in Atlantica, its long-term value, and the strength of the product type,” Alexander Ruiz, chief operating officer of Prestige Companies, said in a statement. The units rent for $1,995 to $3,500 a month, according to Apartments.com. A for-sale listing earlier this year showed a unit priced at $756,000, with $856 in monthly condo association fees. Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Prestige Companies buys back Atlantica at Dania Beach for $27.3M in deed-in-lieu, down from $36.75M sale
124-unit condo conversion by prior owner S2 Dania Property failed; only 6 units sold
Original developer reacquires asset to convert back to rentals post-foreclosure
stories.summary: Prestige Companies, the original developer, repurchased Atlantica at Dania Beach (124 units) for $27.3 million via deed-in-lieu of foreclosure—nearly $10 million below its $36.75 million sale price to S2 Dania Property. S2 acquired the newly completed 2024 apartment community intending to convert to condos but sold only 6 of 124 units, triggering default on its $30 million loan. Prestige now owns 118 of the units.
stories.impact: Dania Beach condo conversion failure signals weak South Florida condo buyer demand despite strong rental fundamentals, likely driven by rising rates, affordability, and buyer hesitation post-2023 rate shock. Prestige's re-entry as rental operator proves rental yields still outstrip condo sales velocity; expect compressed conversion pipelines in South Florida through 2025. Rental market in Dania Beach likely absorbs units efficiently given tourism/seasonal demand; watch for rent trajectory to signal broader coastal Florida multifamily resilience.

stories.title: HFO Investment Real Estate Closes $27M Sale of Luxury Apartments in Fairview
stories.excerpt: HFO Investment Real Estate has completed the $27.3 million sale of Fieldstone Luxury Apartments, a 154-unit community at 20650 NE Halsey St. in Fairview, Oregon. Affordable Housing Associates of Irvine, Calif., sold the property to Benedict Canyon Equities of Los Angeles. The transaction closed at a price of $177,272 per unit. The sale price marks a 30% increase over the $20.8 million the property last traded for in 2015. Tyler Johnson and Cody Hagerman of HFO represented both parties in the transaction. Built in 1997, Fieldstone spans 16 two- and three-story buildings on 8.23 acres. Units average 993 square feet across one-, two- and three-bedroom floor plans. Fieldstone sits in a federally designated Opportunity Zone within walking distance of TriMet bus service and is a short drive from Wood Village Town Center and the Gresham Station transit center. “With major employers like Amazon, FedEx Ground, Boeing and Microchip Technology nearby, Fieldstone has a durable demand base,” said Johnson. bullets: Benedict Canyon Equities acquires Fieldstone Luxury Apartments in Fairview, Oregon for $27.3M ($177k/unit)
154-unit, 1997-built community; 30% price increase over 2015 valuation ($20.8M)
Near Amazon, FedEx Ground, Boeing, Microchip Technology; Opportunity Zone designation, TriMet transit access
stories.summary: Benedict Canyon Equities acquired Fieldstone Luxury Apartments, a 154-unit community in Fairview, Oregon for $27.3 million ($177,272/unit), representing a 30% increase over the property's $20.8 million valuation in 2015. Built in 1997 across 16 buildings on 8.23 acres, the property features one-, two- and three-bedroom units averaging 993 SF. The site sits in a federally designated Opportunity Zone near major employers (Amazon, FedEx Ground, Boeing, Microchip Technology) and TriMet transit service.
stories.impact: Fairview multifamily valuation uplift signals Portland-metro supply tightness and employer-driven demand, especially from logistics-tech corridor (Amazon, FedEx, Boeing expansion). Opportunity Zone tax incentives remain powerful vintage for value-add plays; rising per-unit pricing ($177k vs. historical $135k) suggests tight secondary-market supply and investor confidence in logistics/aerospace job clusters. Watch for similar plays in outer Portland and Vancouver-Clark County as Amazon/FedEx HQ proximity anchors rental demand.

stories.title: Amazon to Invest $100M in Indiana Manufacturing Facility
stories.excerpt: Amazon is planning to invest $100 million to establish an advanced manufacturing facility in Greenwood, Indiana, in a move that would also create 300 jobs. Indiana Governor Mike Braun announced that Amazon will establish a new manufacturing facility in central Indiana by the end of 2028. “Amazon’s decision to locate this facility in Indiana is a powerful testament to the strength of our manufacturing workforce, our world-class infrastructure, and our commitment to creating an environment where businesses of all sizes can grow and thrive,” said Governor Braun. Amazon will purchase and equip a 585,000-square-foot facility at 1175 Collins Road in Greenwood to produce products that power the company’s fulfillment and robotics network across North America. The facility will integrate advanced fabrication, robotic welding, automated powder coating and assembly capabilities. The state’s central location and logistics infrastructure provide direct access to Amazon’s fulfillment network across North America, enabling efficient distribution of manufactured products to facilities nationwide. The post Amazon to Invest $100M in Indiana Manufacturing Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Amazon invests $100M in 585,000 SF advanced manufacturing facility in Greenwood, Indiana
300 permanent jobs; facility operational by end of 2028
Focus on fulfillment robotics, fabrication, assembly; central location leverages Midwest logistics network
stories.summary: Amazon announced a $100 million investment to establish an advanced manufacturing facility in Greenwood, Indiana by end of 2028, creating 300 jobs. The 585,000-square-foot facility at 1175 Collins Road will produce equipment powering Amazon's fulfillment and robotics network across North America, integrating advanced fabrication, robotic welding, and automated assembly. Indiana's central location and logistics infrastructure enable efficient distribution to fulfillment centers nationwide.
stories.impact: Amazon manufacturing hub in Greenwood (Indianapolis metro) signals sustained logistics employment growth and tech-enabled distribution job creation—direct demand driver for renter-occupied workforce housing in Indianapolis and suburban Greenwood. 300 jobs + supply-chain multiplier (vendors, support services) could add 500–800 household demand over build-out; multifamily developers should front-load acquisitions in Greenwood and broader Indianapolis metro submarkets, especially near I-65/I-74 corridors. Manufacturing wage profile (skilled assembly) supports $1,400–$1,800/month rental demand; watch for spec construction leads in 2026–2028.

stories.title: Daniel Management Group Lands Mundelein MF Management Assignment
stories.excerpt: Daniel Management Group (DMG), a Chicago-based real estate firm focused on multifamily investment and management, announced an extension of our relationship with Hawthorne Management Services (HMS) in Mundelein, Illinois. DMG is awarded Lakeside Village Apartments, a community with 144 newly renovated units. The development is located near Hawthorne Mall and one mile from the METRA station. “DMG and HMS have partnered successfully on properties in Mundelein since 2023,” said Roger Daniel, president and founder of Daniel Management Group. “We are looking forward to expanding our presence together and providing more options that maximize the natural beauty of Mundelein’s nearby parks and convenience to shopping, restaurants and Chicago.” Lakeside Village has spacious one- and two-bedroom units that include high-end finishes such as hardwood floors, granite countertops and espresso cabinets. DMG will rebrand the property, upgrade the clubhouse and outdoor areas, and oversee ongoing unit renovations. The post Daniel Management Group Lands Mundelein MF Management Assignment appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Daniel Management Group assumes management of Lakeside Village Apartments in Mundelein, Illinois
144-unit newly renovated property; 1 & 2-bed units with high-end finishes
Near Hawthorne Mall, 1 mile from METRA transit; DMG extends Hawthorne Management Services partnership
stories.summary: Daniel Management Group (DMG), a Chicago-based multifamily firm, secured a management assignment for Lakeside Village Apartments in Mundelein, Illinois, a 144-unit community of newly renovated one- and two-bedroom units near Hawthorne Mall and one mile from METRA station. DMG will rebrand the property, upgrade clubhouse and outdoor areas, and oversee ongoing unit renovations as part of an extension of its relationship with Hawthorne Management Services.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact. Management assignment signals stable Mundelein market fundamentals but no supply or demand signal. Note: If DMG is actively rebranding and upgrading units, this may signal prior underperformance or rent growth opportunity—watch Mundelein submarket for cap-rate compression if value-add is driving investor inflows. Proximity to METRA underscores Chicago exurban transit-oriented multifamily as defensive hold.

stories.title: EquiCap Commercial Completes Sale of Self-Storage Property in Waukegan
stories.excerpt: EquiCap Commercial announced the sale of the H & P Storage located at 2777 N Delany Road in Waukegan, Illinois. The well-established, family-owned self-storage facility features 210 drive-up units across 28,070 net rentable square feet and offers investors a compelling value-add opportunity through operational improvements and revenue optimization. The property features six buildings with a variety of unit sizes. The deal closed a month sooner than contracted. The broker team included Scott Rihm and Jesse Luke, both Partners at EquiCap Commercial. Based in St. Charles, Illinois, EquiCap Commercial is a self-storage advisory group specializing in acquisitions, dispositions, and strategic market guidance with direct market coverage from the Canadian border to the Gulf of Mexico. The post EquiCap Commercial Completes Sale of Self-Storage Property in Waukegan appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: EquiCap Commercial closes sale of H & P Storage in Waukegan, Illinois
210 drive-up self-storage units, 28,070 NSF across six buildings
Deal closed one month ahead of contract; value-add opportunity cited
stories.summary: EquiCap Commercial announced the sale of H & P Storage, a 210-unit self-storage facility in Waukegan, Illinois (2777 N Delany Road) spanning 28,070 net rentable square feet across six buildings. The transaction closed one month ahead of schedule, marketed as a value-add opportunity for operational improvements and revenue optimization.
stories.impact: Minimal impact to multifamily development. Self-storage market in Waukegan (Chicago metro north) shows investor appetite for value-add and accelerated closing; does not signal housing demand or supply trends relevant to apartment development.

stories.title: Extell Seeks $3.8B Financing for Condos on Former ABC-TV Campus
stories.excerpt: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is in talks to lead a $3.8-billion financing for Extell Development’s plan to build condominiums on Manhattan’s Upper West Side at a site that formerly housed the headquarters of the ABC television network. Bloomberg News reported that the financing would be among the largest construction loans ever in the U.S. Extell paid $930 million to acquire the site in 2022 and filed plans last April to build an 86-story tower designed by Robert A.M. Stern Architects. The prolific developer, whose past projects include Central Park Tower and One57, finalized $1.25 billion in financing earlier this month for an 1,800-key hotel in a Times Square project known as the Torch, reported Bloomberg. If it comes together, the financing for the 80 W. 67th St. project would follow the $3.3-billion construction loan that Vornado Realty Trust recently secured for 350 Park Ave., an office tower it’s developing with Rudin and Citadel’s Ken Griffin. The post Extell Seeks $3.8B Financing for Condos on Former ABC-TV Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Extell Development seeks $3.8B construction financing for 86-story condo tower on former ABC-TV campus
JPMorgan Chase leads talks; Upper West Side, 80 W. 67th Street; designed by Robert A.M. Stern
Would rank among largest U.S. construction loans; Extell paid $930M for site in 2022
stories.summary: Extell Development is in talks with JPMorgan Chase to secure a $3.8 billion construction loan for an 86-story condominium tower on Manhattan's Upper West Side at 80 W. 67th Street, the site of the former ABC television network headquarters. If completed, the financing would rank among the largest construction loans in U.S. history. Extell acquired the site for $930 million in 2022 and engaged Robert A.M. Stern Architects for the design.
stories.impact: Largest Manhattan condo construction financing signal since 2019; demonstrates renewed lender appetite for trophy residential (condo) development on prime West Side sites despite rate volatility. $3.8B loan size confirms construction lender confidence in high-end condo pricing power and presale velocity in prime Manhattan—expect ripple effect on other stalled TriBeCa/UWS condo projects seeking financing. Timing suggests Q1 2025 close likely; if realized, signals broader thaw in NYC condo construction financing and validates Extell's development pipeline (Central Park Tower, One57) as institutional collateral. Watch for presale pace post-financing close as market signal of Manhattan condo demand.

stories.title: Greystone Lends $35M on Chicago-Area Apartments Acquisition
stories.excerpt: Isn’t life grand? Multifamily developer Grand Lifestyles has secured $35.4 million of acquisition financing to purchase a multifamily asset in suburban Chicago, Commercial Observer has learned. Greystone closed the Freddie Mac-backed loan to facilitate Grand Lifestyle’s $51.3 million acquisition of The Ponds of Naperville property in Naperville, Ill. from DRA Advisors The financing was originated by Eric Rosenstock, senior managing director at Greystone. “The acquisition market in suburban Illinois is particularly exciting given that it remains one of the few markets experiencing organic rent growth, driven in large part by a lack of new supply and strong underlying multifamily fundamentals,” Rosenstock said in a statement. “The Ponds of Naperville presented Grand Lifestyles with an opportunity to acquire a well-maintained community in an established Chicago-area submarket.” Located at 1331 Modaff Road 30 miles west from Downtown Chicago, the 1988-built property consists of 216 apartments featuring one and two-bedroom units. Community amenities include a clubhouse, recreation room, fitness center, swimming pool, playground, dog park and barbeque area. Grand Lifestyles did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Grand Lifestyles acquires The Ponds of Naperville for $51.3M; Greystone closes $35.4M Freddie Mac loan
216-unit, 1988-built community, 30 miles west of downtown Chicago
Organic rent growth driven by supply scarcity and strong underlying fundamentals in suburban Illinois
stories.summary: Grand Lifestyles secured $35.4 million of Freddie Mac-backed acquisition financing via Greystone to purchase The Ponds of Naperville from DRA Advisors for $51.3 million. The 1988-built community features 216 one- and two-bedroom apartments located at 1331 Modaff Road, 30 miles west of Downtown Chicago. Greystone emphasized the acquisition market in suburban Illinois as "particularly exciting" given organic rent growth driven by limited new supply and strong multifamily fundamentals.
stories.impact: Chicago suburban multifamily cap-rate compression and acquisition pricing signal sustained supply tightness and organic rent growth in Illinois—direct validation of development opportunity for new supply. Freddie Mac willingness to finance 1988-vintage Class B assets at strong LTV suggests lender confidence in Chicagoland fundamentals and NOI trajectory. Watch Naperville and Ring 2 suburbs (Schaumburg, Oak Brook, Downers Grove) for new construction starts in 2025–2026; current valuation levels leave room for 4–5% yield on new development if construction cost inflation moderates. Organic rent growth story trumps new supply risk, supporting development economics.
